question: The resistance of a wire of length L. and area of cross-section A is 0.2 Ω. The resistance of a wire of the same material, but of length 2L and area of cross-section 4A will be:
solution:
The correct answer is __**0.1 Ω**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Given**:

 
 
• The resistance of the first wire (length = L and area = A) is 0.2 Ω.
 
• For the second wire, the length is 2L and the area of cross-section is 4A.
 
 
 
• **Formula**: R=rho (l)/(A), where:
 
 
• R is the resistance,
 
• ρ is the resistivity of the material,
 
• L is the length of the wire,
 
• A is the cross-sectional area of the wire.
 
 
 
• **Calculation:**
 
 
• The resistance of this second wire is given by: R'=ρ (2L)/(4A) =ρ (L)/(2A)
 
• Now, compare the two resistances: R' = (1)/(2) ρ (L)/(A)
 
• Since, R=rho (l)/(A)=0.2Ω
 
• We can substitute this into the equation for R': R' = (1)/(2) * 0.2 Ω = 0.1 Ω
 
• Thus, the resistance of the second wire will be 0.1 Ω.
